# Emblor v2 `2.0.0-alpha.0`

Emblor v2 is now available for alpha evaluation through the npm `next` channel:

```bash
npm install emblor@next
# or
pnpm add emblor@next
```

This release is a deliberate breaking change from v1. It publishes one headless `emblor` package with a root-only compound API: `EmblorRoot`, `EmblorLabel`, `EmblorTagList`, `EmblorTag`, `EmblorTagText`, `EmblorInput`, `EmblorTagRemove`, and `EmblorClear`. Values are `string[]`; Root owns committed and draft state, validation, form participation, announcements, and focus coordination; consumers own markup, styling, keys, and optional integrations.

## Alpha expectations

- The v2 vertical-slice architecture is frozen, but this alpha is not semver-stable. Contract-restoring fixes remain expected, and a public-contract change requires an explicit superseding decision.
- React 18 and React 19 are supported. Repository and release verification use Node 24 with Node 22 compatibility coverage; the published package does not impose a Node engine.
- The package is intentionally headless. Autocomplete, suggestions, cmdk, popovers, sorting, drag-and-drop, Shadcn, Tailwind, CVA, styling runtimes, addons, and feature subpaths are excluded from core.
- The production website remains on v1 while the v2 documentation site is planned separately.
- `latest` remains `1.4.8`; this prerelease is available through `next` only.

## Migration

Start with the [v1-to-v2 migration guide](https://github.com/JaleelB/emblor/blob/main/packages/emblor/MIGRATION.md) in the source tree or the `MIGRATION.md` shipped in the npm tarball. The generated [package changelog](https://github.com/JaleelB/emblor/blob/main/packages/emblor/CHANGELOG.md) records the breaking release entry.

## Feedback

Use the [alpha issue forms](https://github.com/JaleelB/emblor/issues/new/choose) and select the category that best matches your finding:

- runtime behavior;
- accessibility or browser compatibility;
- TypeScript or package ergonomics;
- documentation or migration gaps;
- a proposed change to the frozen contract.

Include the exact Emblor version, React/Node/browser environment, reproduction, impact, expected behavior, severity, and target alpha where the form requests them. Contract proposals must name the affected decision; an issue is not approval to change the frozen API.

Please do not report or solve an alpha defect by unpublishing the version. Published versions are immutable release evidence; fixes should ship as a subsequent verified alpha.
